title: High-resolution TVD, ENO and WENO reconstruction

items.title: Finite-volume MUSCL, nodal ENO2 and WENO5 reconstruction conventions
items.statement: On a uniform grid, distinguish cell averages from nodal values and define the scalar MUSCL/minmod, nodal ENO2 and left-biased cell-average WENO5-JS/WENO-Z face reconstructions, including their scalar-advection update and characteristic-system interpretation.

references.title: Chi-Wang Shu, Essentially Non-Oscillatory and Weighted Essentially Non-Oscillatory Schemes for Hyperbolic Conservation Laws, complete lecture notes
references.locator: §§2.1.1 and 2.2.1–2.2.2, PDF pp. 3–21: reconstruction from cell averages, ENO stencil selection, WENO convex weights and Jiang–Shu indicators.

references.title: Guang-Shan Jiang and Chi-Wang Shu, Efficient Implementation of Weighted ENO Schemes
references.locator: §§2–4, PDF pp. 3–18: WENO candidate stencils, smoothness indicators, nonlinear weights and optimal linear combination.

references.title: Jérôme Droniou, A Beginner’s Course in Finite Volume Approximation of Scalar Conservation Laws, complete lecture notes
references.locator: §§3.1–3.3, PDF pp. 31–35: piecewise-linear MUSCL cell reconstruction, minmod slopes and the fully discrete CFL distinction.

items.title: A monotone linear one-step advection scheme cannot be second order at noninteger CFL
items.statement: For a fixed noninteger Courant number, no finite-stencil translation-invariant conservative linear one-step scheme for scalar advection is both monotone and second-order accurate.

references.title: Randall J. LeVeque, Numerical Methods for Conservation Laws, full textbook
references.locator: Ch. 16 §16.1, Theorem 16.1, printed pp. 174–175 (PDF pp. 187–188): a linear monotonicity-preserving method is at most first order.

items.title: The selected nodal ENO2 quadratic reconstructs the face to third order
items.statement: For nodal data from a C3 scalar function on a uniform grid, either quadratic selected by the stated ENO2 divided-difference rule approximates the intervening face value with error O(h^3), including ties.

references.title: Chi-Wang Shu, Essentially Non-Oscillatory and Weighted Essentially Non-Oscillatory Schemes for Hyperbolic Conservation Laws, complete lecture notes
references.locator: §§2.1.1 and 2.2.1, PDF pp. 3–17: polynomial interpolation and ENO divided-difference stencil selection.

items.title: The WENO5 ideal linear weights reproduce quartics at the right face
items.statement: The ideal WENO5 weights (1/10, 6/10, 3/10) combine the three displayed cell-average candidate functionals into a fifth-order right-face reconstruction.

references.title: Chi-Wang Shu, Essentially Non-Oscillatory and Weighted Essentially Non-Oscillatory Schemes for Hyperbolic Conservation Laws, complete lecture notes
references.locator: §2.2.2, PDF pp. 18–21: optimal linear weights, candidate cell-average reconstructions and fifth-order consistency.

references.title: Guang-Shan Jiang and Chi-Wang Shu, Efficient Implementation of Weighted ENO Schemes
references.locator: §§2–3, PDF pp. 3–13: fifth-order WENO candidate functionals and their optimal linear combination.

items.title: MUSCL/minmod face states are second order on smooth monotone data
items.statement: If a C3 scalar profile is strictly monotone near a uniform-grid cell, its minmod-limited MUSCL face states approximate the exact face values with error O(h^2).

references.title: Jérôme Droniou, A Beginner’s Course in Finite Volume Approximation of Scalar Conservation Laws, complete lecture notes
references.locator: §§3.1–3.3, PDF pp. 31–35: cell-centered piecewise-linear MUSCL reconstruction and minmod selection.

items.title: Direct forward-Euler MUSCL/minmod is TVD under the sharp two-thirds CFL bound
items.statement: For the unchanged direct linear-advection forward-Euler MUSCL/minmod update, finite-variation bi-infinite or periodic data have nonincreasing total variation for |a|Δt/h≤2/3, including equality; the bound is sharp throughout the original CFL range through one.

references.title: Jérôme Droniou, A Beginner’s Course in Finite Volume Approximation of Scalar Conservation Laws, complete lecture notes
references.locator: §§3.1–3.3, PDF pp. 31–35: equation (3.1.2) is the direct MUSCL update, equation (3.3.1) is minmod, and equation (3.3.8) gives the sufficient CFL restriction. The variation estimate, signed-velocity reduction and sharpness are proved locally.

items.title: The specified direct MUSCL/minmod flux update is not TVD at CFL one
items.statement: The direct reconstructed-upwind forward-Euler update in the PE02 design is not total-variation diminishing for every CFL number in [0,1].

references.title: Jérôme Droniou, A Beginner’s Course in Finite Volume Approximation of Scalar Conservation Laws, complete lecture notes
references.locator: §3.3, PDF pp. 32–35, especially condition (3.3.8): the minmod MUSCL update requires an additional CFL restriction; the local finite data below directly refute the PE02 CFL-one assertion.

items.title: Fixed-epsilon WENO-JS and WENO-Z face reconstructions are fifth order
items.statement: For C5 data and a fixed positive dimensionally scaled epsilon, the displayed WENO-JS and WENO-Z cell-average reconstructions have fifth-order face error as h tends to zero.

references.title: Guang-Shan Jiang and Chi-Wang Shu, Efficient Implementation of Weighted ENO Schemes
references.locator: §§2–3, PDF pp. 3–13: Jiang–Shu indicators, normalized nonlinear weights and fifth-order smooth-region reconstruction.

references.title: Chi-Wang Shu, Essentially Non-Oscillatory and Weighted Essentially Non-Oscillatory Schemes for Hyperbolic Conservation Laws, complete lecture notes
references.locator: §2.2.2, PDF pp. 18–21: accuracy condition for convex WENO weights and the fifth-order cell-average construction.

references.title: Andrew K. Henrick, Tariq D. Aslam and Joseph M. Powers, Mapped weighted essentially non-oscillatory schemes: Achieving optimal order near critical points
references.locator: §4.3–4.5, printed pp. 552–554: the WENO-JS order depends on epsilon and resolution; the critical-point analysis distinguishes the fixed-epsilon limiting regime from small scale-dependent epsilon. The source studies finite-difference fluxes; this item proves the finite-volume face-state claim locally.

title: High-resolution TVD, ENO and WENO reconstruction — Examples

items.title: Minmod clips the slope at a smooth quadratic maximum
items.statement: For cell averages of u(x)=1-x^2 on a uniform grid centered at zero, minmod sets the central slope to zero and reconstructs both adjacent face states as the central average.

items.title: Unlimited centered reconstruction creates new extrema on a step
items.statement: Unlimited centered slopes with the reconstructed upwind forward-Euler update can increase total variation and create values outside the initial range even at CFL one half.

items.title: MUSCL and WENO reconstruct a translating affine profile exactly
items.statement: For u(x,t)=x-at on a uniform grid, minmod MUSCL and every normalized WENO variant reconstruct the upwind face value exactly and the conservative update advances the cell averages exactly.

items.title: A first-order critical point exposes WENO-JS epsilon scaling
items.statement: For cell averages of u(x)=x^2+x^3 at the face x=0, the WENO-JS choice epsilon=h^4 gives a fourth-order face error, while fixed epsilon and the displayed WENO-Z comparison retain at least fifth order.

references.title: Andrew K. Henrick, Tariq D. Aslam and Joseph M. Powers, Mapped weighted essentially non-oscillatory schemes: Achieving optimal order near critical points
references.locator: §§4.2–4.5, printed pp. 552–554: the WENO-JS order depends on epsilon and resolution at critical points. The source analyzes finite-difference fluxes; the cell-average face calculation here is performed explicitly.

references.title: Guang-Shan Jiang and Chi-Wang Shu, Efficient Implementation of Weighted ENO Schemes
references.locator: §3, PDF pp. 7–13: the WENO-JS smoothness indicators and normalized weights used in the calculation.

items.title: Positive-state Burgers shock and the monotone finite-volume baseline
items.statement: For the Burgers Riemann datum 1 to 0, the entropy shock travels at speed 1/2; the positive-state Godunov flux is monotone and the batch-29 convergence theorem applies to its first-order finite-volume baseline.

references.title: Jérôme Droniou, A Beginner’s Course in Finite Volume Approximation of Scalar Conservation Laws, complete lecture notes
references.locator: §§2.2.2–2.3.3, PDF pp. 15–23, and §3.3, pp. 32–35: positive-state Burgers Godunov flux, monotone finite-volume convergence context and minmod MUSCL reconstruction.
